When the soft keyboard opens, the wayland window:
Inset (surface shrinks above the keyboard, client reflows)
Overlay (keyboard floats over the window, surface unchanged)
Display zoom (whole wayland window, applies immediately):
Window scaling (when a fixed-size window is resized, applies immediately):
Auto attach (daemon launches the host window automatically when a wayland window is created; off = the window waits for a binder SURFACE from its app):
Stretch (fill the window, aspect may distort)
Scale XWayland windows with display zoom :
Initial window size (first-frame placeholder before Android sizes the window, applies to new windows):
Compositor backend (on = SC/HWC: wayland layers are composed by SurfaceFlinger, zero-copy scanout when possible; off = per-window GL renderer fallback. Applies to windows attached from now on):
The daemon turns the window whose title matches into a headset view: barrel pre-distortion per eye plus reprojection with the phone IMU. Needs the SC backend OFF (the GL path does the warping).
Eye layout (how the headset image is packed into the window):
Single eye (one image fills the screen)
Frame rate published to the headset (0 = follow the panel):
Render target per eye (0 = derive from the eye layout and the panel):
Field of view, total per eye (degrees):
Render scale — per-eye resolution relative to the nominal size (1000 = 1.0x, lower = faster, blurrier):
Lens barrel distortion k1 (0 = none; raise until straight lines look straight through the lenses):
Lens barrel distortion k2 (second order, only needs a touch):
Chromatic aberration correction (0 = off; raise if edges fringe red/blue):
Pose prediction (milliseconds of head motion extrapolated past the newest sample; 0 = off):
6DoF: if a file anland-xr-pose-ext appears next to anland-xr-pose (written by an ARCore/OpenXR bridge), its poses replace the phone IMU automatically. Without it the session is 3DoF.

A compositor such as KWin, Weston, Sway or Mutter running inside one anland window. Session mode gives it FULLSCREEN|MAXIMIZED on every configure and pins it to the panel, so it treats the host as a monitor.
